messages.subject: initial values for survival/abundance model
parts:
Hello, I'm running a robust design survival model that includes a data augmentation part to estimate abundance.  If I use the known.state.cjs and the cjs.init.z functions from the WinBUGS books I can get the survival part to run, but when I add the augmentation part, things fall apart.  The initial values don't seem to satisfy jags.  Thoughts?  code is attached.  Y is vectored in this code, I have another version where y is a array (more typical) and again things run for the survival part but not the augmentation part.

Robin

messages.subject: AW: initial values for survival/abundance model
parts:
Hi Robin,

 

Have you looked at the code of this paper ?

 

Rankin, R.W., Nicholson, K.E., Allen, S.J., Krützen, M., Bejder, L. & Pollock, K.H. ( 2016) A Full‐capture hierarchical bayesian model of Pollock's closed robust design and application to dolphins. Frontiers in Marine Science, 3, 25.

 

I think they have some clever inits function there.

 

Best regards  -- Marc

Von: hmec...@googlegroups.com [mailto:hmec...@googlegroups.com] Im Auftrag von Robin Russell

Betreff: initial values for survival/abundance model

 

Hello, I'm running a robust design survival model that includes a data augmentation part to estimate abundance.  If I use the known.state.cjs and the cjs.init.z functions from the WinBUGS books I can get the survival part to run, but when I add the augmentation part, things fall apart.  The initial values don't seem to satisfy jags.  Thoughts?  code is attached.  Y is vectored in this code, I have another version where y is a array (more typical) and again things run for the survival part but not the augmentation part.

 

Robin
